svg.aria-label: Azure credential model after the change: the customer adds a federated credential naming this tenant's GitHub environment, and each run carries two tokens with that subject, one exchanged with Entra ID to sign in and one presented to the platform, which releases the tenant's application secrets once. No secret travels in the dispatch.

g.text: Azure — credential model AFTER (workload identity federation)
No secret is created or shared, and none travels in the dispatch. The tenant's subject gets the run into the customer's subscription and gets it the tenant's application secrets.
CONTROL PLANE (platform)
GITHUB ACTIONS RUN
CUSTOMER AZURE SUBSCRIPTION
1 · ONBOARDING (ONCE PER TENANT)
the wizard shows issuer, subject and audience — nothing travels back
Wizard issues the tenant ID first
Form: subscription ID, tenant ID, client ID,
LLM key, Pinecone key — and no secret
A random UUID, generated when the page
opens, names the credential the customer
must create before pressing Deploy.
No Azure call is made, and none is needed.
Not involved
The tenant's GitHub environment is
created automatically on the first run,
so there is nothing to configure here.
Federated credential, added by the customer
On an app registration or a user-assigned
managed identity. No secret is created.
issuer token.actions.githubusercontent.com
subject repo:<owner>/<repo>:environment:
tenant-<tenant ID>
audience api://AzureADTokenExchange
2 · EVERY DEPLOYMENT AND TEARDOWN
Dispatch, then release on request
GITHUB_PAT, long-lived. Inputs: tenant_id,
deployment_id and non-secret settings only.
Releases the LLM, Pinecone and signer
secrets once, to a run whose token proves:
this repo · tenant-<id> environment · the
Azure workflow · an active, unclaimed deploy.
Nothing secret in the dispatch payload.
Two tokens, one subject
environment: tenant-<tenant ID>
aud api://AzureADTokenExchange
→ Entra ID signs the run in
aud ai-chatbot-platform:tenant-secrets
→ the platform releases the secrets
Neither token is accepted in the
other's place.
Entra ID decides, then terraform apply
Subject matches the credential → an access
token valid for 60–90 minutes.
Any other subject → login refused, with
nothing created; the platform reports the
subject it expected.
The released secrets are written to the
tenant's Key Vault and app settings.
3 · WHAT THE PLATFORM HOLDS
No Azure credential, and nothing that expires
Stored: the LLM key, the Pinecone key and the docs-signer secret (AES-256-GCM), released once per deployment as in band 2 and erased at teardown.
Identifiers only for the subscription: subscription ID, Entra tenant ID, client ID. None of them grants access without a matching token.
Closed: a database compromise no longer implies a cloud compromise, and there is no secret to rotate, expire or resend through CI (see fig-22).
4 · REVOCATION AND BLAST RADIUS
Revocation
The customer deletes the federated credential.
It takes effect at once, needs no platform action,
and leaves nothing behind to clean up.
They can also list their identity's credentials to see
exactly which chatbots may sign in.
Where the trust moved
To the deploy repository and to GitHub as token
issuer: whoever can change these workflows can act in
accounts that trust the platform, and receive the
secrets a run is released (Limitation #8).
Narrower than a decryptable secret, but a real dependency.
Requires GitHub Environments, which private repositories get on paid plans. Without them the token carries no environment, the subject does not match, and the deploy stops at sign-in.
